subject: SDK graceful-fallback exemption + mutual action items
messages:
From: Judy Lin <judy@fleetops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: FleetOps Procurement <procurement@fleetops.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDK graceful-fallback exemption + mutual action items

Hi Marcus,

We've run into a production issue while using the Redwood SDK in our long-document summarization pipeline. When the platform routes to a smaller fallback variant (during peak load) we see token duplication and occasional truncated streams that break our downstream commit step. Attached is a trimmed log with the error window (fleetops_error_snippet.log).

Immediate ask: can Redwood grant a temporary SLA/behavior exemption for graceful-fallback routing for FleetOps while we complete an SDK patch? This is customer-impacting for several active accounts.

We'd like a mutual action plan (timeline + acceptance criteria) and a list of telemetry/metrics Redwood needs from us to validate the fix. Procurement has asked for any contract language we might need for the exemption window.

Notes:
- Problem frequency: ~2-3% of requests during fallback events
- Repro: long prompts (>8k tokens) with streaming + prefix caching enabled

Thanks — appreciate quick coordination.

—
Judy Lin
Head of Integrations, FleetOps
judy@fleetops.com
(415) 555-0197
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Judy Lin <judy@fleetops.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK graceful-fallback exemption + mutual action items

Judy — thanks for the precise repro and log snippet. I dug into the trace and see the same duplication around the fallback handoff; likely an interaction between our prefix/KV cache and variant-switching during an inflight streaming session.

Looping in Tessa (Sales Engineering) to coordinate the MAAP and acceptance criteria, and Logan (Runtime) for the technical triage. Marissa for any contractual nuance.

Proposed immediate steps from our side:
1) Redwood provides a short-term exemption (behavioral SLO note) for FleetOps fallback routing while we test a field SDK patch in canary with you.
2) We produce a MAAP CSV with milestones and telemetry signals required (attached: maap_draft.csv).
3) Triage runbook + fallbacks/playbook we will share (planned attachment: fallback_playbook.pdf).

Can you confirm the earliest windows you can accept a canary (non-prod first, then a small % in prod) and whether you need an NDA/contract amendment before we start? Procurement is CC'd.

Action items:
- Judy: confirm canary windows + procurement lead contact
- Tessa: draft MAAP and telemetry checklist
- Logan: scope runtime change and estimated time-to-fix

I'll capture these in the HubSpot deal and share the DocuSign link for any temporary SLA redline once we align.

Best,
Marcus
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Judy Lin <judy@fleetops.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK graceful-fallback exemption + mutual action items

Thanks everyone — quick technical plan and a few product asks so we scope correctly.

Summary of what we'll do (high level):
- Short-term: enable a canary SDK flag that disables automatic variant fallback for streams over a configured token threshold. This gives FleetOps control while we validate the runtime fix.
- Medium-term: runtime patch to make variant-switch atomic w.r.t. KV cache state and streaming offsets.

Telemetry we need from FleetOps (minimum):
- request_id, route_id, model_variant_in, model_variant_out, timestamps for switch, and per-chunk token sequence hashes
- a sample of 10 failed streams and 10 matched-successful streams for comparison

Product asks / questions for roadmap input: 
- Would FleetOps accept a config toggle per-route (SDK flag) that opts out of automatic fallback? This is different from the per-account global escape hatch.
- If yes, we can target an SDK patch and publish a canary build within 4 business days after we get the MAAP approved.

Canary rollout plan (proposal):
1) Non-prod integration window (2 hours) — validate no duplication with synthetic load
2) Prod small % (0.5% traffic) for 48 hours — monitor token duplication metric and tail latency
3) Gradual ramp to full traffic when metrics stable for 72 hours

Acceptance criteria (for green):
- duplication rate <= 0.2% on canary traffic
- no increase in 95th latency beyond 10% of baseline
- no new error class in runtime logs related to KV cache misses

Quick code snippet for the SDK flag we propose (for your engineers):

// SDK usage example
RedwoodClient client = new RedwoodClient({ fallbackPolicy: 'opt_out', fallbackThresholdTokens: 8000 });
client.stream({ model: 'rwd-medium', prompt: longPrompt });

Attachments: fallback_playbook.pdf — contains the step-by-step canary checklist and monitoring dashboards we will instrument.

Marcus — can you and Logan confirm ETA for the runtime patch path (rough estimate is fine) so I can include it in the MAAP?

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
From: Judy Lin <judy@fleetops.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: FleetOps Procurement <procurement@fleetops.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SDK graceful-fallback exemption + mutual action items

Marcus / Tessa — thanks for the clear plan. FleetOps can accept the per-route SDK opt-out toggle as an initial mitigation. We can run the non-prod window next Tuesday (09/14) 02:00–04:00 PT and a small prod test Wed 09/15 01:00–49:00 PT (0.5% traffic) if that works for your ops calendar.

Procurement notes: we need a 30-day temporary amendment reflecting the exemption and the MAAP milestones before we flip the opt-out in prod. I've attached procurement's redline placeholder (sla_redlines.docx) — please send a DocuSign-ready version and the MAAP CSV so we can get legal signoff.

Also attaching a concise list of the 10 sample failed streams from our environment (we'll share the full traces via a secure bucket if needed).

Looking forward to the canary.

—
Judy Lin
Head of Integrations, FleetOps
